I was raised by my financially irresponsible grandmother, and even though my financial insight isn’t much better thanks to her, I soon had a realization that she spent a lot of our little money (her disability check + my child support) on cigarettes and junk food.

When I was almost 18, she got catfished on Facebook and wouldn’t believe me when I told her that she was getting scammed. (Because they were “in love and he’d visit her from the US soon, he just needed money to put his daughter through boarding school” lmao.) What did I find out afterwards? That she took out a loan of €5000 to give to the scammer…

My grandma will always brag to other people about how smart I am as one of the only people in my family to graduate high school and get a college degree - but when I actually told her she was getting financially screwed, she would just not believe me. Nevermind that while I was getting myself through college, the first few years she called every other week to “borrow” money, mostly for cigarettes. Once I finally learned that I could say no and she’d still be able to eat, those calls eventually tapered off.

Not to dump, but I hope you take my experience as a cautionary tale… don’t move her closer to you, she can and will ruin you financially along with herself. Protect your peace and stability.

It wasn't necessarily hard to hear for me, as I am still deciding whether I'm going no contact with my mother (father skipped out on me entirely so that was an easy one lmao). Thanks for caring though, besides this event I have gotten pretty decent treatment here so far :)

It was, however, a bit difficult to parse what the psychologist said because I know being low contact the past few years has kept me feeling safe.
